assumption: The 2019 NPE -> 2021 LGE relationship between national and local voting carries over to 2024 NPE -> 2026 LGE
why: Only one observed national-to-local pair on comparable geography
evidence: None yet beyond the fit itself; the Johannesburg model notes one of its two transitions was Covid-affected
effect_if_wrong: Systematic bias for parties whose national and local appeal diverge (local civics, MK)

assumption: Province and council shock sizes: 0.35 and 0.15 on the log-share scale
why: Chosen by the pre-registered 2021 backtest on the corrected, common-case metric (L037-L038)
evidence: Lowest seat CRPS of 24 settings; established-party coverage 85.6% at 90%, 50.3% at 50%. Neighbouring settings are close. One election only
effect_if_wrong: Intervals too wide or too narrow in 2026 if its political weather differs from 2021's

assumption: Excessive-seat rule applies only when a party's ward wins strictly exceed its entitlement
why: Originally an assumption about zero-ward parties under an equal-or-greater reading
evidence: IEC 2021 calculations for all 25 Western Cape councils reproduced exactly with the strict trigger; the equal-or-greater reading failed 6 (L019)
effect_if_wrong: n/a: resolved by evidence

assumption: OTHER is split into real parties with fixed weights from recent elections
why: OTHER is not a party and must not win seats as a bloc
evidence: None
effect_if_wrong: Seat counts for very small parties are rough

assumption: Local-only parties keep their 2021 LGE share, before shocks
why: They are not on national ballots, so 2024 carries no signal for them
evidence: None
effect_if_wrong: New or collapsed civic movements are missed entirely

assumption: Registered voters per 2026 VD = MDB REGPOP, which is a 2024 snapshot
why: 2026 VD-level registration is not published
evidence: Johannesburg model SOURCES.md
effect_if_wrong: Differential registration growth since 2024 is ignored

assumption: Until candidate lists are parsed, every modelled party contests every ward
why: Contestation data not yet ingested
evidence: None
effect_if_wrong: Overstates ward vote for parties with thin ward coverage (cf. PA 52/135 JHB wards in 2021)
status: closed for WC when candidate lists parse (L018)

assumption: Both ballots share one turnout per VD; spoilt ballots ignored in seat maths
why: Simplicity
evidence: Seat maths uses valid votes only, so spoilt ballots do not matter there
effect_if_wrong: Negligible for seats

assumption: Independent ward candidates are not modelled separately
why: Few independents won Western Cape wards in 2021 (to be verified)
evidence: None yet
effect_if_wrong: A strong local independent would be missed

assumption: District councils (40% PR ballot) are not forecast
why: Scope for v0.1
evidence: n/a
effect_if_wrong: Site covers local and metro councils only

assumption: Where local knowledge and the IEC certified candidate list disagree about whether a party is standing, the model follows the certified list until the dispute is settled
why: The certified list is what appears on the ballot paper; an unverified claim should not silently change a forecast
evidence: Disputes are recorded with both sources in party_status_2026.csv; the first two (L020) were resolved in favour of the list (L021)
effect_if_wrong: A party wrongly excluded or included changes that council's forecast

assumption: Voters of a party that stood before but is not standing in 2026 are shared among the standing parties in proportion to those parties' support in the same voting district
why: A neutral default: we have no evidence yet on where such voters go
evidence: None; local knowledge or by-election results could replace it council by council via swing_priors.csv
effect_if_wrong: Matters most where the absent party was large: Karoo Gemeenskap Party 11% (Prince Albert), GOOD 8% (Beaufort West)

assumption: For parties with no fitted national-to-local translation, b = 1 and the local premium a is uncertain: a prior from the fitted parties' premiums, updated by precision with by-election evidence where at least 3 wards exist
why: No 2019 national vote to learn from (the PA was not on the 2019 provincial ballot)
evidence: PA: 14 by-election wards since the 2024 national election give +0.20 ± 0.19; combined +0.12 ± 0.17 (L023). NCC, PMC, ATM: prior only
effect_if_wrong: For parties on the prior alone, the prior mean (−0.32) may be wrong for locally organised parties, as it was for the PA

assumption: By-election evidence is taken only from by-elections after the 2024 national election
why: Earlier by-elections predate the 2024 baseline they are compared with
evidence: Placebo parties are consistent with zero after 2024 but drift before it (systematic error 0.35); including them moves the PA estimate from +0.20 to −0.18 (L023)
effect_if_wrong: A different window changes the PA's premium, and its seats in councils such as Beaufort West, Matzikama, Laingsburg and Prince Albert

assumption: Each party's learned local premium carries over from the previous national-to-local cycle at half strength
why: Premiums carry information but overshoot for individual parties (the DA's 2014 -> 2016 premium over-predicted it by 53 seats in 2021)
evidence: Full premiums beat zero premiums (L028, L037); halved premiums with slopes at 1 beat full premiums on ward Brier with no cost on seats (L040)
effect_if_wrong: A party whose local premium has changed is mis-predicted; halving limits the damage

assumption: A newcomer's council share follows a party-weighted regression on past Western Cape newcomers (ward coverage, standing in every ward, breadth, council size, history elsewhere in the province), and is taken proportionally from all other parties
why: The 2026 lists name 122 newcomer cases but give no information on their strength beyond where they stand
evidence: v1 (classes) was switched off in L043. v2 passed the pre-registered 2021 backtest at the adopted settings (seat CRPS 0.379 against 0.400, 90% interval of the difference -0.034 to -0.009; coverage 87.9%) and check C20 (L045-L046). The backtest fit (2016 only) has no party-wide component; the 2026 fit does (rho 0.33)
effect_if_wrong: Newcomers systematically stronger or weaker than past ones; votes taken unevenly (e.g. mostly from one party)

assumption: The SACP uses a sourced prior (council share median 0.8%, 90th percentile 2.5%); other newcomers standing in 11+ councils use the class prior
why: The class prior for wide newcomers is dominated by the PA's 2021 surge; the SACP has a poll bound
evidence: Ipsos Jun-Jul 2026: SACP below 2% nationally; scaled by the ANC's weaker Western Cape base (maintainers' judgement, L041). No poll evidence for the Afrika Mayibuye Movement
effect_if_wrong: If the SACP is stronger than the Ipsos bound implies, its share, and the ANC's loss to it, are understated

assumption: Slopes of the national-to-local translation are fixed at 1 (the national spatial pattern carried unsquashed), with intercepts re-estimated
why: Fitted slopes are attenuated by sampling noise; the errors-in-variables correction made seats worse
evidence: Pre-registered ward experiment (L040): slopes at 1 with halved premiums was best on ward Brier with no cost on seats; corrected slopes were worst on seats
effect_if_wrong: If a party's spatial pattern genuinely changes between national and local elections, it is not captured

assumption: Polls are not used as model inputs; they are a published cross-check
why: Before 2024, Western Cape polls missed the provincial result by large margins in both directions, so there is no consistent bias to correct
evidence: DA errors from -11 (Ipsos, late 2023) to +9 points (SRF, July 2023, turnout-modelled); EFF up to +10; SRF March 2024 -2 on the DA (L041-L042)
effect_if_wrong: If the 2026 polls are more accurate than earlier ones, information that could narrow the forecast is left unused

assumption: Each party's learned local premium is measured against the national vote interpolated to the local election's date, between the national elections either side, not against the earlier national election
why: Measured against the earlier election, the premium absorbs swing between the national and local elections and carries it into 2026 as if it were local
evidence: Pre-registered 2021 backtest (L045): seat CRPS 0.4014 against 0.4050, ward Brier 0.151 against 0.157, DA 54.7% against 54.7% actual (53.4% before). Against it: council control right in 19 of 25 councils rather than 21, and the ANC over-predicted slightly more (24.9% against 20.5%)
effect_if_wrong: If swing between elections is itself informative about local strength, interpolation discards real signal; the fraction assumes change was linear between the national elections

assumption: Ward and district noise is centred on each party's log share, with one spread for every party
why: The simplest symmetric uncertainty on the log-share scale; the spreads are estimated from 2019 -> 2021 residuals
evidence: Under test (L047): the share decomposition shows this lowers a dominant party's expected share by several points (convexity), yet the 2021 backtest predicted the DA's provincial share almost exactly with it. The spreads are dominated by small parties' sampling noise (O12)
effect_if_wrong: A dominant party's share is understated, most of all where it dominates: the DA in Cape Town and its strongholds
